family.name: Wallenberg family and foundations

ranking.promotionReason: Al Maktoum family did not carry enough direct fresh evidence to replace the incumbent.

executiveAssessment.whatWasFound: No new wrongdoing finding is asserted. The family is elevated because the leading lanes overlap with documented access across Industrial ownership, Banking, Defence industry, Telecommunications, Pharmaceuticals, Research funding, Board networks.
executiveAssessment.whyItMatters: The Wallenberg Foundations hold decisive voting influence in Investor AB, with the largest foundation alone holding more than 42 percent of votes as of June 2026. The ecosystem states that the three largest foundations collectively hold 50 percent of Investor's votes. Family members hold senior board positions while Investor uses board participation across a portfolio spanning finance, defence, industrials, pharmaceuticals and technology.
executiveAssessment.howItFits: The family lane tests whether legal succession, voting pools, foundations, holding companies, trustee powers, appointments or repeated gatekeeping preserve institutional access across generations. The mechanism—not the surname—is the evidence.
executiveAssessment.whatItPointsToward: A focused review of industrial ownership, banking, defence industry, telecommunications and whether documented control rights or appointments connect the family to current policy, capital or infrastructure developments.
executiveAssessment.alternativeExplanation: The ecosystem demonstrates exceptional corporate continuity and board access, but it is not equivalent to control of the Swedish state or every company in which Investor owns shares.
executiveAssessment.whatItDoesNotProve: The evidence does not support claims that the Wallenbergs secretly direct Sweden, NATO or European institutions as a unified private government.
executiveAssessment.evidenceStrength: E4–E5 — structural public records; no direct new allegation
